scene_objective: Sera opens the archive and recognizes the pre-Ruusan Veranthos containment protocol, while Ben and Desh connect that hidden record to the later Ruusan Reformations; Torin and Kael arrive as distinct human presences rather than exposition sources.
opening_mode: Sera crosses to the archive console and her fingers find the activation sequence from muscle memory — a thousand years old and still faster than Ben's modern training

key_beats.beat_description: Sera activates the archive console with an ancient access code from muscle memory — former lieutenant, lock-breaker, and unwilling instrument of Gavran's protocol, using competence that now indicts the system that used her

Torin pulls the Veranthos protocol index into the display, adding a story-shaped inflection that warms lived pre-Ruusan facts with remembered names and campaign texture without pretending to know the later reforms
Ben or Desh cross-references the Veranthos protocol language against the later Ruusan Reformations Ben knows from Jedi training and the Order his father rebuilt

Kael reaches past Sera to correct one Gavran designation — his first voluntary contribution — replacing architect with keeper/custodian of the concealed Veranthos protocol, precisely and without emphasis because the difference between a person and an institutional title matters to him
Sera names only the Veranthos protocol's function: private penance-and-containment. Ben supplies the later public-reform frame and feels the connection land before he understands it
Ben's close-third registers what each of the three has just become for him: Sera the instrument, Torin the keeper, Kael the correction

turning_point.trigger: Ben understands that the later Ruusan Reformations did not create the Veranthos protocol; they buried and carried it. The known public demilitarization of the Jedi after the New Sith Wars remains true
turning_point.shift: Ben understands that the later Ruusan Reformations did not create the Veranthos protocol; they buried and carried it. The known public demilitarization of the Jedi after the New Sith Wars remains true

closing_beat: Sera names the Veranthos protocol as containment and penance. Ben supplies the word Reformations himself. Sera does not say what the penance was for. She does not need to. Ben can read the rest of it off her face

emotional_arc.shift: Absorbing shock -> intellectual vertigo -> moral reckoning with institutional history

anti_patterns: Do not open with a flashback or exposition dump explaining the Reformations.
Do not have the survivors deliver the revelation as a lecture or coordinated explanation.
Do not let Sera, Torin, Kael, or Veraine speak as eyewitnesses to the post-Ruusan public Reformations; they were sealed before the Ruusan aftermath.
Do not have Torin or Sera say they helped write the Reformations index, negotiated the reforms, moved younglings, or remember post-Ruusan legislation.

Do not have Sera characterize the later public settlement before Ben does; no survivor line should say 'the settlement was built to carry the wound,' 'what came after,' or equivalent Reformations analysis.
Do not soften the institutional fact with apology or context—let it land clean.
Do not claim the public Ruusan Reformations were false or merely philosophical; preserve canon that they were real demilitarization, centralization, and Republic oversight after the New Sith Wars.
Do not imply Gavran authored the public Reformations or their official settlement terms; he is the custodian/engineer of the concealed Veranthos protocol beneath them.
Do not describe the archive language as Old Galactic Standard or as predating Basic; use archaic Basic, High Galactic legal script, or pre-Reformation administrative Basic.
Do not call the anchors volunteers as a group; some were captured, coerced, or repurposed, and Gavran is the only central keystone.
Do not use collective consent language for the anchors or survivors: no 'we signed up,' 'we agreed,' 'we volunteered,' or 'we chose this' unless the sentence is explicitly limited to Torin alone.
Do not leave 'thirteen anchors' ambiguous; if the count appears, specify twelve chamber-bound anchors plus Gavran as the central keystone.
Do not describe Ben as a conventional Old Order youngling; refer to the Jedi history he inherited through his Order, his father's Order, or later Jedi training.

Do not invent precise Reformation implementation details such as exact negotiation durations, youngling relocation logistics, or specific oversight mechanisms beyond the broad public reforms named here.
Do not imply the modern Jedi Order forgot something it once formally taught; Ben may struggle with archaic text because it is rare, specialized, or outside his training.
Do not arrive at clinical articulation of the institutional lie; let Ben feel it before he understands it.
Do not flatten the survivor voices into a unified exposition vector; they must emerge as distinct persons.
The scene works only if the survivor voices separate immediately. Land the institutional shock cleanly, then stop before the room tries to answer everything.
